column1: # Retrospective bench points — tagged GitHub artifacts (rakupp-macos-universal)
# re-run on ONE machine in one sitting: 2026-08-21, Darwin 25.5, Apple Silicon.
# rakudo v2026.07 and perl v5.34 measured once in the same sitting as fixed
# references. Methodology: 7 runs, first discarded, minimum kept; output
# correctness-gated before timing. gen-dashboard merges these as GAP-FILL
# only: a kernel a tag's own committed tables carry keeps its mined numbers.
# CAVEAT (2026-08-21, added when the release tables were re-measured): this
# whole sitting runs ~1.4x slow against the Darwin 24.6 machine that every
# OTHER series in the dashboard was measured on. Re-running v3.6.0's hashfill
# there gives interp 178.0 / native 63.7 (vs 249.9 / 96.4 here) while perl
# gives 95.5 vs 86.0 — perl was FASTER in this sitting and Raku++ slower, so
# it is not machine speed: something handicapped the Raku++ binary, most
# likely the x86_64 slice of the universal artifact running under translation.
# run-bench's arch guard reads `file -b`, which reports arm64 for a universal
# binary whichever slice executes, so it could not have caught this.
# Consequence: the hashfill series is internally consistent (one machine, one
# sitting) but sits on a different scale from the nine mined series, and its
# last point (main) is now measured on Darwin 24.6 — so the drop at that point
# is part real (ValueHash) and part scale. Re-run this table on Darwin 24.6
# with per-arch artifacts to make the series comparable.
